name: Typhon
note: Typhon and Echidna, and the brood the heroes were sent against

Echidna.note: Half fair-cheeked woman, half monstrous serpent, who lives in a hollow rock and dies neither of age nor sickness. Mother of nearly every monster the heroes fight. Gives echidna, the spiny anteater, which is part mammal and part reptile-seeming. Theog. 295-305

people.Ladon: The hundred-headed serpent coiled round the golden apples of the Hesperides. Theog. 333-335
people.Typhon: Gaia's last child, by Tartaros, born to avenge the Titans: a hundred serpent heads, and voices of every kind -- bulls, lions, hissing, speech. Zeus burned him down with the thunderbolt and pinned him under Aitna, and the mountain still smokes. Gives typhoon, though only partly: the English word is a collision of Greek typhon with Arabic tufan and Chinese tai fung. Theog. 820-868
people.Kerberos: The fifty-headed hound of Hades, bronze-voiced, who fawns on those who enter and eats those who try to leave. Herakles' twelfth labour. Roman: Cerberus. Gives cerberus, a savage doorkeeper. Theog. 310-312
people.Orthros: The two-headed hound of Geryon, killed by Herakles on the way to the cattle. Theog. 293, 309
people.Hydra: The Lernaian water-snake, which grew two heads for each one cut; Herakles' second labour, won only by burning the stumps. Gives hydra, and the freshwater animal named for its regrowth. Theog. 313-318
people.Chimaira: Lion in front, goat in the middle, serpent behind, breathing fire; killed by Bellerophon from the air on Pegasos. Gives chimera, chimerical, and in genetics an organism of two cell lines. Theog. 319-325
people.Sphinx: The strangler -- from sphingein, to squeeze, which also gives sphincter. She set the riddle at Thebes and threw herself from the rock when Oidipous answered it. Theog. 326-329

NemeanLion.name: Nemean Lion
NemeanLion.note: The lion of Nemea, whose hide no weapon could pierce; Herakles throttled it and wore the skin thereafter. Theog. 327-329

people.Pegasos: The winged horse, sprung from Medousa's neck when Perseus cut off her head. He carried Bellerophon against the Chimaira and threw him when he tried to ride to heaven; Zeus keeps him now and he carries the thunderbolt. Gives pegasus, and the constellation. Theog. 280-286
people.Chrysaor: Of the golden sword, born with Pegasos from Medousa's neck. Theog. 280-283
people.Geryon: Three-bodied king of Erytheia, whose red cattle were Herakles' tenth labour. Theog. 287-294

unions.note: Poseidon lay with Medousa in a soft meadow among spring flowers; when Perseus struck her head off, the two children leapt out. Recorded on the Gorgon record, which stands for all three sisters. Theog. 278-283
